req.title: Reject wrong method on /delete
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than DELETE on /delete.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /delete must return HTTP 405 for any method other than DELETE. We need: (1) a positive test confirming DELETE returns 200, (2) negative tests confirming non-DELETE methods return exactly 405, and (3) boundary tests covering the full set of common HTTP methods. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (405 vs 200), testing both sides of the method-allowed boundary, and covering multiple wrong-method variants to catch operator/constant mutations in Flask's method routing.

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_method_returns_200():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'args' in data
    assert 'origin' in data

tests.name: test_all_non_delete_methods_return_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Methods GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, HEAD are all non-DELETE
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Iterate over all non-DELETE HTTP methods and send each to /delete
trace: R-HTTPBIN-011: All methods other than DELETE must return 405 on /delete
BVA: boundary between allowed (DELETE=200) and disallowed (all others=405)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_non_delete_methods_return_405():
    non_delete_methods = [
        ('GET', client.get),
        ('POST', client.post),
        ('PUT', client.put),
        ('PATCH', client.patch),
    ]
    for method_name, method_fn in non_delete_methods:
        r = method_fn('/delete')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"{method_name} /delete expected 405, got {r.status_code}"
        assert r.status_code != 200, f"{method_name} /delete must not return 200"
    # Confirm DELETE itself is still 200 (boundary: the one allowed method)
    r_delete = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r_delete.status_code == 200

test_all_non_delete_methods_return_405()

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_response_payload_structure():
    r = client.delete('/delete?foo=bar')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in data, f"Missing key: {key}"
    assert data['args'] == {'foo': 'bar'}

test_delete_response_payload_structure()
